item.title: Why Must Executables in Current Directory Use './' Prefix in Unix-like Shells
item.description:
“Why Must Executables in Current Directory Use ‘./’ Prefix in Unix-like Shells”

When attempting to execute a script or program situated in the present working directory (CWD) on systems like Linux or macOS, users often find that simply typing the filename fails, requiring a prefix like ./. Why does the shell mandate this explicit notation? This behavior stems from security considerations inherent in the shell’s command resolution process, specifically how it interacts with the $PATH environment variable.
